MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 25, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ruesch at 5:00
p.m., on February 25, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00
p.m. on February 20, 2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray Community
and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum (arrived at 5:10 pm)
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation. Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9: Janice Kronik Gath, et. al v. Mission Viejo OCSC Case No. 30-2024-
  01376969-CU-MC-CJC

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 pm Mayor Ruesch recessed the meeting to Closed Session. Mayor Ruesch
reconvened the meeting at 6:04 pm with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  February 25, 2025
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that there was no reportable actions were taken.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Working Wardrobes for 35 years of Empowering Individuals and Strengthening
  our Community

  Mayor Ruesch presented proclamation to CEO Bonni Pomush of Working Wardrobes and received
  presentation from Working Wardrobes.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

June Anderson, M.V.: Voiced concerns of the woody acacia on Alicia at the north end of the golf course
and asked that it be trimmed due to being a fire hazard.

Karen Warren, M.V.: Voiced her concerns about the dead plants and trees on Jeronimo between gate 3
of Casta del Sol and Silleros and asked that the City inspect this fire hazard.

Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Questioned if the landscape contracts will abide by Governor Newsom’s
order to ban gas powered equipment and replaced with electric powered equipment.

Peggy O’Neill, M.V.: Spoke on the federal funding cuts and asked the City Council how they plan to
mitigate this problem.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Spoke on the past districting process and pointed out that each Council Member is
equal and when a sitting council member is denied serving as Mayor or Mayor Pro Tem that district of
registered voters is being denied equal access in the community.

Kristen Wilcox, M.V.: Spoke out on ICE raids and asked the City Council to not allow them within our
City and asked that Mission Viejo be ordained a Sanctuary City.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

18. La Paz Bridge/Road Widening (CIP 01756)

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Council Members voiced their concerns about the length of time this project has taken, as well as
  the federal funding.

  Director Chagnon explained that he did not see a problem with the federal funding coming through.
  He also reported the reasons for the delay of the project which had to do with the bridge overhang
  decking was completely deteriorated underneath and could not support the new median barrier rail.
  This caused the demolition of the deck overhand that had to be reconstructed.

  Tom Moore, M.V.: Complimented city staff and consultants on this project with weathering the
  frustrations by the public. He voiced his concerns of Marguerite & La Paz indicating more lighting
  is needed and that he hopes this area doesn’t become another Oso or Alicia Parkway.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to (1) authorize
  the City Manager to approve Construction Contract Change Order 4 with Flatiron West, Inc. in
  the amount of $2,161,669; (2) authorize the City Manager to approve Amendment 2 with Arcadis
  U.S., Inc. in the amount of $282,649 for construction management services; and (3) adopt
  Resolution 25-03 Amending the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Budget for Costs Related to Capital
  Improvement Project CIP 01756.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez

City Council Minutes  6  February 25, 2025
 Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell gave an update from the Olympic Committee pertaining to the visits of
OCEANA, Australia and New Zealand. He stated there is quite a bit of action going on in Southern
California with these Nations securing their training facilities from San Diego to Ventura. He mentioned
that during the Olympic games a lot of National Committees will have hospitality homes, and it appears
that the popular city is Culver City. He said to stay tuned for more information as it becomes solidified.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley thanked Council Member Goodell for his update on the upcoming Olympics in
2028. She thanked Director Mark Nix and his team for the successful Oso Fit 5K this past weekend.
She gave kudos to Aumee Frey and Barbara Swanson. Council Member Kelley also thanked Mark Nix
for providing the equipment this evening to be able to stream the Council Meeting, as well as Eric Winter
and our I.T. Department.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez circled back to a couple of public comments this evening and asked if we
could hear more about ICE raids and the instructions of our police at the next meeting. She voiced her
concerns about getting pulled over because she is brown. Council Member Vasquez also would like to
hear more at an upcoming meeting about any contingency plans if federal funding falls through. She
also commented on electric equipment for the landscaping contracts and how this will be incorporated
in the future. She highlighted her 20th wedding anniversary in Napa this past weekend. Lastly, she
mentioned that her Girl Scout Troop earned their democracy badge after touring City Hall.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum asked for an update on the Sober Living Recovery Home situation at a future
meeting. She stated that there is some legislation coming up and that the responsibility and funding of
the task force has been successfully transferred to the Association of California Cities. Council Member
Bucknum commented on the federal funds and also asked for a status update at a future meeting. She
referenced that with concern of the fires and the pending completion of the Los Angeles Convention
Center that Mission Viejo will assist with the 2028 Olympics if venues are needed. She asked the police
chief to highlight the event at the Elks Lodge and the recognition of Deputy Cody Eliason. Lastly, she
attended the Oso Fit 5K which was a great event and gave thanks to all the volunteers.

Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch thanked staff for pulling together the audio and visual for the meeting this evening. He
stated that he met with Congresswoman Young Kim and about five or six Mayors. He had the
opportunity to collaborate with the Mayor of Brea who also has a mall managed by Simon Properties.
Mayor Ruesch and City Manager Lister met with the president of Saddleback College which was very
productive regarding the 2028 Olympics. He also attended Oso Fit 5K and with a last minute change to
the countdown music by William Tell Overture, got everybody excited to start the race. Mayor Ruesch
concluded with the following quote: “Success is neither magical, nor mysterious. Success is the natural
consequences of consistently applying basic fundamentals”.
